content:
Assuming you mean **Winterthur, Switzerland**, I can draft a simple schedule, but I would **not** use “Friday and Saturday nights until 11pm” as the default basis.

A 14-year-old is a **child under Swiss child/youth work rules**. Parental consent alone does not allow a café employer to schedule a 14-year-old for evening/night work. You should check the following before putting him on a roster:

1. **School days**  
   If he is still in compulsory schooling, work is generally only allowed on days when he has **no school**. Friday is likely a school day, so he may not be allowed to work Friday at all.

2. **Night work**  
   Work after **22:00** is normally prohibited for under-18s unless a cantonal authority explicitly permits it. A shift until **23:00** would include at least one hour of night work, so it should only be used if you have **written permission** covering those exact hours.

3. **Suitable tasks**  
   A 14-year-old should not serve/sell alcohol, operate hazardous equipment, lift heavy loads, or work alone in the evening. He should be supervised and given simple, age-appropriate tasks.

4. **Permit/confirmation**  
   For a café job, especially if the hours are in the evening or cross 22:00, you should get written confirmation from the competent cantonal authority — in Canton Zurich, typically the **Kantonales Arbeitsinspektorat** or the relevant child/youth work authority.

---

## Recommended simple schedule if you do **not** have a special night-work permit

This is the safer version. It avoids Friday if he has school, avoids night work, and keeps the shifts short.

| Day | Start | Break | Finish | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Friday | 15:00 | 17:00–17:30 | 19:00 | Only if Friday is a full school-free day for him. If he has school on Friday, do not schedule him. |
| Saturday | 14:00 | 16:00–16:30 | 18:00 | Only if he has no school/exam that day. Finish early to avoid evening/night issues. |

Simple rules to attach:

- No work during school hours or before exams.
- No serving or selling alcohol.
- No operating dangerous machines.
- No heavy lifting.
- Must be supervised by an adult employee.
- Keep total working time reasonable, e.g. no more than 4 hours per day.
- Keep a simple timesheet and pay him as agreed.

---

## If you receive written permission for evening work until 23:00

Use this **only if** the written permission specifically allows a 14-year-old to work in your café on Friday and Saturday until 23:00, including the time after 22:00.

| Day | Start | Break | Finish | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Friday | 19:00 | 20:00–20:30 | 23:00 | Only if permitted. Finish at 23:00 sharp. Ensure safe transport home. |
| Saturday | 19:00 | 20:00–20:30 | 23:00 | Only if permitted. No extra shifts or late closing tasks. |

Even in that case, I would limit him to short shifts and avoid tasks such as:

- serving alcohol,
- handling large amounts of cash alone,
- cleaning/operating hot or dangerous equipment,
- staying late if the café becomes crowded or difficult to manage.

---

## Simple written schedule/agreement you could adapt

You could use something like this internally:

```text
Casual work schedule — under-16 employee

Employee name: ______________________
Date of birth: ______________________
Parent/guardian: ______________________
Parent phone: ______________________

Employer: ______________________
Address: ______________________

Role: Café assistant, age-appropriate tasks only.

Working days:
Friday: 15:00–19:00, only if no school.
Saturday: 14:00–18:00, only if no school/exam.

Break:
30 minutes after 2 hours.

Permitted tasks:
- simple table service support
- helping with cleaning under supervision
- light non-hazardous café tasks

Not permitted:
- serving or selling alcohol
- operating hazardous machines
- heavy lifting
- working alone in the evening
- working during school hours or before exams

Parent/guardian consent:
I confirm that my child may work within the above limits and I will be available for contact if needed.

Parent signature: ______________________
Date: ______________________

Employer signature: ______________________
Date: ______________________
```

---

In short: I would **not** put him on a normal Friday/Saturday shift until 23:00 based only on his parents saying it is fine. The safe route is to keep him on short, supervised, school-free-day shifts and only use evening/night hours if you have explicit written permission from the competent authority.
